summary: Uranchimeg Tsultemin works in history and archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. She earned her Ph.D. from UC Berkeley (~2003–2009), later lecturing there (~2009–2018), and held posts at the National University of Mongolia, Yonsei University, IUPUI, and the University of Iceland.

Urs App specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Fribourg, Gymnasium St. Antonius Appenzell, and Temple University, under Yoshitaka Iriya, Richard DeMartino, and Seizan Yanagida. His posts include Hanazono University and École française d'Extrême-Orient.

Ute Hüsken is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She completed her dissertation at the University of Göttingen (~1987–1995) under Heinz Bechert and held a post at Heidelberg University around 2003.

V. Raghavan was an Indologist who completed his Ph.D. at the University of Madras (1931–1934) under S. Kuppuswami Sastri. He served on the University of Madras faculty from around 1935 to 1973, including as Head of the Sanskrit Department.
Vaibhav Singh works in history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed his PhD at the University of Reading by 2017 and held an attested post there in 2018.
Vajragupta is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He served as director at the Birmingham Buddhist Centre in 1997 and was attested as Director of the Triratna Buddhist Community in 2010.

Valdo H. Viglielmo was a specialist in Japanology and philosophy. After studying at the University of Pennsylvania and Harvard University, he held posts at Meiji Gakuin University, Princeton University, and as a professor at the University of Hawaii (~1965–2000).

Valeria Gazizova specializes in Tibetology, religious studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She completed her Master's thesis at the University of Oslo under the supervision of Per Kvaerne (attested 2009).
Vasily Radlov worked in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the Humboldt University of Berlin (~1854–1858) and held a post at the Kunstkamera (~1894–1918).

Vasudev Vishnu Mirashi was a scholar of Indology and history and archaeology. He served as Principal and Professor of Sanskrit at Morris College and the Government Vidarbha Institute, later holding an honorary professorship at Rashtrasant Tukadoji Maharaj Nagpur University (~1957–1966).

Vasudev Vishwanath Gokhale worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Sinology, completing his PhD at the University of Bonn by 1930. He held academic posts at Fergusson College, Visva-Bharati University, and the University of Delhi.

Vasudha Narayanan is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. She studied at the University of Madras, University of Mumbai, and Harvard University, and became Distinguished Professor of Religion at the University of Florida around 1982.
Verity Harte is a philosopher who studied at the University of Cambridge (~1986–1994). She held posts at King's College London (~1997–2006) and Yale University (~2006).

Vesna A. Wallace specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies. She completed her doctoral dissertation at UC Berkeley and held posts at UC Berkeley, the University of Oxford as Numata Chair, and UC Santa Barbara as Professor.
Victor B. Lieberman is a historian who studied at Yale University (~1963–1967) and SOAS University of London (~1969–1976). He held a post at the University of Michigan around 1984.

Victor Chan works in Tibetology. He studied at the University of Chicago and served as Executive Director of the Contemporary Tibetan Studies Program at the University of British Columbia, attested in 2005.

Victor Forte specializes in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He earned his Ph.D. from Temple University by 2004 and was attested as an assistant professor of religious studies at Albright College in 2007.

Victor H. Mair specializes in Sinology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He studied at Dartmouth College, SOAS, and Harvard University, and held posts at Harvard University (~1976–1979) and the University of Pennsylvania (from ~1979).
Victor Henry was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He held posts at École Centrale de Lille (~1872–1888) and the University of Paris (1888).

Victor Turner worked in religious studies and related fields. He studied at University College London and the University of Manchester, later serving as chair of the Committee on Social Thought at the University of Chicago (~1968–1977).
